source_text: Αὕτη γὰρ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἡ φύσις, ἄνωθεν καὶ κατὰ γνώμην τοῦ ποιήσαντος συγκεκληρωμένην ἔχουσα τὴν ἀνωμαλίαν, ἀνώμαλον ἔχει τὴν ζωὴν καὶ τὴν διαμονήν, ποτὲ μὲν ὕπνῳ ποτὲ δὲ θανάτῳ διακοπτομένην καὶ ταῖς καθ᾿ ἑκάστην ἡλικίαν μεταβολαῖς, οὐκ ἐμφαινομένων ἐναργῶς τοῖς πρώτοις τῶν ὕστερον ἐπιγινομένων. Ἢ τίς ἂν ἐπίστευσεν, μὴ τῇ πείρᾳ δεδιδαγμένος, ἐν ὁμοιομερεῖ καὶ διαπλάστῳ τῷ σπέρματι τοσούτων καὶ τηλικούτων ἀποκεῖσθαι δυνάμεων ἢ τῶν ταύτῃ ἐπισυνισταμένων καὶ πηγνυμένων ὄγκων διαφοράν, ὀστέων φημὶ καὶ νεύρων καὶ χόνδρων, ἔτι δὲ καὶ μυῶν καὶ σαρκῶν καὶ σπλάγχνων καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σώματος μερῶν; Οὔτε γὰρ ἐν ὑγροῖς ἔτι τοῖς σπέρμασι τούτων ἔστιν ἰδεῖν οὐδέν, οὔτε μὴν τοῖς νηπίοις ἐμφαίνεταί τι τῶν τοῖς τελείοις ἐπιγινομένων, ἢ τῇ τῶν τελείων ἡλικίᾳ τὰ τῶν παρηβηκότων, ἢ τούτοις τὰ τῶν γεγηρακότων. Ἀλλὰ δὴ καίτοι τῶν εἰρημένων τινῶν μὲν οὔθ᾿ ὅλως τινῶν δὲ ἀμυδρῶς ἐμφαινόντων τὴν φυσικὴν ἀκολουθίαν καὶ τὰς τῇ φύσει τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπιγινομένας μεταβολάς, ὅμως ἴσασιν ὅσοι μὴ τυφλώττουσιν ὑπὸ κακίας ἢ ῥαθυμίας περὶ τὴν τούτων κρίσιν, ὅτι δεῖ πρῶτον μὲν γενέσθαι τῶν σπερμάτων καταβολήν, διαρθρωθέντων δὲ τούτων καθ᾿ ἕκαστον μέρος καὶ μόριον καὶ προελθόντων εἰς φῶς τῶν κυηθέντων ἐπιγίνεται μὲν ἡ κατὰ τὴν πρώτην ἡλικίαν αὔξησις, ἥ τε κατ᾿ αὔξησιν τελείωσις, τελειωθέντων δὲ ὕφεσις τῶν φυσικῶν δυνάμεων μέχρι γήρως, εἶτα πεπονηκότων τῶν σωμάτων ἡ διάλυσις. Ὥσπερ οὖν ἐπὶ τούτῳ, οὔτε τοῦ σπέρματος ἐγγεγραμμένην ἔχοντος τὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ζωὴν ἢ μορφὴν οὔτε τῆς ζωῆς τὴν εἰς τὰς πρώτας ἀρχὰς διάλυσιν, ὁ τῶν φυσικῶς γενομένων εἱρμὸς παρέχει τὴν πίστιν τοῖς οὐκ ἐξ αὐτῶν τῶν φαινομένων ἔχουσι τὸ πιστόν, πολὺ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος ἐκ τῆς φυσικῆς ἀκολουθίας ἀνιχνεύων τὴν ἀλήθειαν πιστοῦται τὴν ἀνάστασιν, ἀσφαλέστερος ὢν καὶ κρείττων τῆς πείρας πρὸς πίστωσιν ἀληθείας.
thought_title: Natural sequence grounds belief in resurrection
orientation: Athenagoras is arguing that the observable natural sequence of human development—from seed to growth to decay—gives rational ground for believing in resurrection, even where the stages are not visible in advance.
pass_a_gloss: For this is the nature of humans, having from above and according to the purpose of the maker the irregularity allotted, it has an irregular life and continuance, at one time by sleep at another by death being interrupted and by the changes at each age, the later things not being clearly shown in the first things. Or who would have believed, not having been taught by experience, that in the homogeneous and formable seed so many and so great powers are stored up, or the difference of the masses that are formed and compacted from it, I mean of bones and sinews and cartilages, and further of muscles and fleshes and entrails and the remaining parts of the body? For neither in the seeds while still moist is it possible to see any of these things, nor indeed is any of the things that come upon the mature shown in infants, or in the age of the mature the things of those past their prime, or in these the things of the aged. But indeed although of the things mentioned some do not at all and some faintly show the natural sequence and the changes that come upon the nature of humans, nevertheless those know who are not blinded by wickedness or carelessness concerning the judgment of these things, that first there must come to be a deposit of the seeds, and when these have been articulated part by part and member by member and the conceived have come forth to light, there comes upon them the growth according to the first age, and the completion according to growth, and when they have been completed a decline of the natural powers until old age, then when the bodies have labored the dissolution. Just as therefore in this case, although neither the seed has the life or form of humans inscribed in it nor the life has the dissolution into the first principles, the chain of things that happen naturally provides the belief to those who do not have the trustworthy from the appearances themselves, much more does reason, tracing out the truth from the natural sequence, confirm the resurrection, being more secure and stronger than experience for the confirmation of truth.

lemmas.gloss: having been conceived, carried in womb

choices.why: Keeps the perfect participle's force: the irregularity is a fixed allotment from the maker, not a mere possession.
rejected: having received irregularity as its lot

choices.why: The verb means cutting through or breaking off; 'interrupted' preserves the sense that life's continuance is broken by sleep and death.
The noun from καταβάλλω means a laying down or casting down; 'deposit' keeps the concrete sense of seed being laid down.
The noun means a letting down or relaxation; 'decline' fits the context of natural powers diminishing after maturity.
The word means a connected series or sequence; 'chain' preserves the image of linked natural events.
The middle voice of πιστόω means to make trustworthy or establish as credible; 'confirms' fits the argument that reason establishes the resurrection.

pass_b_english: For this is the nature of human beings: from the beginning, by the purpose of the Maker, it has been allotted an irregular course, and so its life and continuance are irregular. At one time they are interrupted by sleep, at another by death, and by the changes that come with each stage of life, since what comes later is not clearly visible in what comes first. Who would ever have believed, without being taught by experience, that in seed which is uniform and still being formed there lie stored up so many and such great powers, or that from it would arise such different masses as they are joined and compacted together—I mean bones, sinews, cartilage, and also muscles, flesh, entrails, and the remaining parts of the body? For none of these can be seen while the seeds are still fluid, nor is anything that belongs to the mature visible in infants, nor what belongs to those past their prime visible in the mature, nor what belongs to the aged visible in those past their prime. And yet, although some of these things show the natural sequence and the changes that come to human nature either not at all or only dimly, all who are not blinded by wickedness or carelessness in judging these matters know that first the deposit of the seeds must take place; then, when they have been articulated into each part and member and those conceived have come forth into the light, there follows growth in the first stage of life, then completion through growth, and after completion a decline of the natural powers until old age, and finally, when the bodies have grown weary, their dissolution. Just as in this case—where the seed does not have the life or form of human beings written into it, nor does life have its dissolution back into its first elements written into it—the chain of natural events gives faith to those who do not find what is trustworthy in the appearances themselves, so much more does reason, tracing out the truth from the natural sequence, confirm the resurrection, since it is more reliable and stronger than experience for establishing the truth.

last_rejected.quote: since what comes later is not clearly visible in what comes first
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ ἐμφαινομένων ἐναργῶς τοῖς πρώτοις τῶν ὕστερον ἐπιγινομένων
last_rejected.why: Greek says later things not visible in earlier, not vice versa; English reverses the relationship
last_rejected.fix: since what comes later is not clearly visible to those who come first
last_rejected.ruling: τοῖς πρώτοις governs ἐμφαινομένων; 'later things not visible in first' is what English says—no reversal.

last_rejected.quote: or that from it would arise such different masses as they are joined and compacted together
last_rejected.source_quote: ἢ τῶν ταύτῃ ἐπισυνισταμένων καὶ πηγνυμένων ὄγκων διαφοράν
last_rejected.why: Greek has 'difference of masses joined and compacted therefrom,' not 'from it would arise such different masses as they are joined'
last_rejected.fix: or the difference of the masses joined and compacted together from it
last_rejected.ruling: ταύτῃ = 'therefrom'; 'from it would arise such different masses' faithfully renders τῶν...ὄγκων διαφοράν.

last_rejected.quote: nor what belongs to those past their prime visible in the mature, nor what belongs to the aged visible in those past their prime
last_rejected.source_quote: ἢ τῇ τῶν τελείων ἡλικίᾳ τὰ τῶν παρηβηκότων, ἢ τούτοις τὰ τῶν γεγηρακότων
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'in the prime of the mature, the things of those past their prime, or in these the things of the aged'—English reverses direction of visibility
last_rejected.fix: nor in the mature the things of those past their prime, nor in these the things of the aged
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly says things of past-prime not visible in mature, aged not in past-prime—matches Greek dative direction.

last_rejected.quote: since it is more reliable and stronger than experience for establishing the truth
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀσφαλέστερος ὢν καὶ κρείττων τῆς πείρας πρὸς πίστωσιν ἀληθείας
last_rejected.why: Greek says reason is more reliable and better than experience, not 'more reliable and stronger'—κρείττων means 'better/superior', not 'stronger'
last_rejected.fix: since it is more reliable and better than experience for establishing the truth
last_rejected.ruling: κρείττων ranges 'stronger/better/superior'; 'stronger' is valid, not a meaning change.
